question: Should OpenClaw officially support capturing and optionally replaying local edits inside an installed package's `dist` tree during self-update?
rationale: The code and proof can establish technical safety, but they cannot decide whether unsupported installed-package mutations should become a long-term public update contract with a new CLI option and recovery lifecycle.

options.title: Support bounded opt-in replay
options.body: Accept preserve-by-default behavior, the explicit trusted replay flag, strict fail-closed validation, and documented recovery semantics.

options.title: Preserve recovery bundles only
options.body: Keep capture and user-visible recovery reporting but remove replay support and the CLI option.

options.title: Decline override support
options.body: Close the draft and continue treating installed `dist` edits as outside OpenClaw's supported update contract.

recommendation.title: Support bounded opt-in replay
recommendation.body: Accept preserve-by-default behavior, the explicit trusted replay flag, strict fail-closed validation, and documented recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the assigned owner and the strongest historical contributor signal across the central update surfaces, so he is best positioned to accept or reject the product contract.
